db-15.description: Description: Enterprise-level market segmentation analysis with rate type distribution, customer segment analysis, and comprehensive market intelligence. Use Case: Market Segmentation Platform - Rate Type Distribution Analysis for Market Analysts Business Value: Comprehensive market segmentation analysis showing rate type distributions, customer segment analysis, and market intelligence. Enable
db-15.complexity: Deep nested CTEs (6+ levels), market segmentation, distribution analysis, customer segment analysis, aggregations
db-15.expected_output: Market segmentation analysis with rate type distributions and customer segment metrics.
db-15.sql:
WITH rate_type_distribution AS (
    SELECT
        er.rate_type,
        er.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        s.region,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_id) AS rate_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.utility_id) AS utility_count,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS avg_rate,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS median_rate
    FROM electricity_rates er
    INNER JOIN states s ON er.state_id = s.state_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY er.rate_type, er.state_id, s.state_name, s.region
),
market_segmentation AS (
    SELECT
        rtd.*,
        SUM(rtd.rate_count) OVER (PARTITION BY rtd.state_id) AS total_rates_in_state,
        SUM(rtd.rate_count) OVER (PARTITION BY rtd.region) AS total_rates_in_region,
        (rtd.rate_count::NUMERIC / SUM(rtd.rate_count) OVER (PARTITION BY rtd.state_id)) * 100 AS state_market_share,
        (rtd.rate_count::NUMERIC / SUM(rtd.rate_count) OVER (PARTITION BY rtd.region)) * 100 AS region_market_share
    FROM rate_type_distribution rtd
)
SELECT
    rate_type, state_id, state_name, region,
    rate_count, utility_count,
    ROUND(CAST(avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS avg_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(median_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS median_rate,
    total_rates_in_state, total_rates_in_region,
    ROUND(CAST(state_market_share AS NUMERIC), 2) AS state_market_share,

db-15.title: Cross-Utility Rate Comparison with Competitive Positioning
db-15.description: Description: Enterprise-level cross-utility rate comparison with competitive positioning, utility benchmarking, and comprehensive competitive analysis. Demonstrates production patterns used by competitive intelligence platforms and utility comparison systems. Use Case: Competitive Analysis Platform - Cross-Utility Rate Comparison for Energy Consultants Business Value: Comprehensive cross-utility rate comparison showing competitive positioning, utility benchmarking, and competitive analysis. Enab
db-15.complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), cross-utility comparisons, competitive positioning, benchmarking, complex joins
db-15.expected_output: Cross-utility rate comparison with competitive positioning and benchmarking.
db-15.sql:
WITH utility_rate_comparison AS (
    SELECT
        er1.utility_id AS utility_1_id,
        uc1.utility_name AS utility_1_name,
        er1.state_id,
        er1.rate_code_id,
        er1.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS utility_1_rate,
        er2.utility_id AS utility_2_id,
        uc2.utility_name AS utility_2_name,
        er2.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS utility_2_rate,
        er1.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh - er2.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS rate_difference,
        CASE
            WHEN er2.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh > 0 THEN
                ((er1.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh - er2.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) / er2.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) * 100
            ELSE NULL
        END AS rate_difference_percentage
    FROM electricity_rates er1
    INNER JOIN utility_companies uc1 ON er1.utility_id = uc1.utility_id
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er2 ON er1.state_id = er2.state_id AND er1.rate_code_id = er2.rate_code_id
    INNER JOIN utility_companies uc2 ON er2.utility_id = uc2.utility_id
    WHERE er1.is_current = TRUE AND er2.is_current = TRUE
        AND er1.utility_id < er2.utility_id
),
competitive_positioning AS (
    SELECT
        urc.*,
        CASE
            WHEN urc.rate_difference < -0.01 THEN 'More Competitive'
            WHEN urc.rate_difference > 0.01 THEN 'Less Competitive'
            ELSE 'Similar'
        END AS competitive_position
    FROM utility_rate_comparison urc
)
SELECT
    utility_1_id, utility_1_name, utility_2_id, utility_2_name,
    state_id, rate_code_id,
    ROUND(CAST(utility_1_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS utility_1_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(utility_2_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS utility_2_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(rate_difference AS NUMERIC), 6) AS rate_difference,
    ROUND(CAST(rate_difference_percentage AS NUMERIC), 2) AS rate_difference_percentage,
    competitive_position
FROM competitive_positioning
ORDER BY state_id, ABS(rate_difference) DESC;

db-15.complexity: Deep nested CTEs (8+ levels), rebate stacking, optimization algorithms, combination analysis, maximum savings calculations
db-15.expected_output: Rebate stacking optimization with maximum savings calculations.
db-15.sql:
WITH rebate_combinations AS (
    SELECT
        sra.state_id,
        sra.utility_id,
        sra.zip_code,
        sra.total_federal_incentives_usd,
        sra.total_state_incentives_usd,
        sra.total_utility_incentives_usd,
        sra.total_combined_incentives_usd,
        sra.federal_incentive_count,
        sra.state_incentive_count,
        sra.utility_incentive_count
    FROM solar_rebate_aggregations sra
    WHERE sra.calculation_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'
),
system_scenarios AS (
    SELECT system_size_kw, system_cost_per_watt
    FROM (VALUES (5.0, 3.0), (10.0, 3.0), (20.0, 2.8)) AS scenarios(system_size_kw, system_cost_per_watt)
),
maximum_savings_calculation AS (
    SELECT
        rc.*,
        ss.system_size_kw,
        ss.system_cost_per_watt,
        ss.system_size_kw * ss.system_cost_per_watt * 1000 AS system_cost,
        rc.total_combined_incentives_usd AS total_rebates,
        (ss.system_size_kw * ss.system_cost_per_watt * 1000) - rc.total_combined_incentives_usd AS net_cost,
        (rc.total_combined_incentives_usd / (ss.system_size_kw * ss.system_cost_per_watt * 1000)) * 100 AS rebate_percentage
    FROM rebate_combinations rc
    CROSS JOIN system_scenarios ss
)
SELECT
    state_id, utility_id, zip_code, system_size_kw,
    ROUND(CAST(system_cost AS NUMERIC), 2) AS system_cost,
    ROUND(CAST(total_rebates AS NUMERIC), 2) AS total_rebates,
    ROUND(CAST(net_cost AS NUMERIC), 2) AS net_cost,
    ROUND(CAST(rebate_percentage AS NUMERIC), 2) AS rebate_percentage,
    federal_incentive_count, state_incentive_count, utility_incentive_count
FROM maximum_savings_calculation
ORDER BY rebate_percentage DESC, state_id;

db-15.title: Rate Trend Forecasting with Predictive Analytics
db-15.description: Description: Enterprise-level rate trend forecasting with predictive analytics, trend prediction, and comprehensive forecasting models. Demonstrates production patterns used by forecasting platforms and predictive analytics systems. Use Case: Forecasting Platform - Rate Trend Prediction for Energy Market Forecasters Business Value: Comprehensive rate trend forecasting showing trend predictions, forecasting models, and predictive analytics. Enables energy market forecasters to predict rate trends
db-15.complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), time-series forecasting, predictive analytics, trend prediction, statistical modeling
db-15.expected_output: Rate trend forecasting with predictive analytics and trend predictions.
db-15.sql:
WITH historical_rate_trends AS (
    SELECT
        her.utility_id,
        her.rate_code_id,
        her.state_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', her.effective_date) AS rate_month,
        AVG(her.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS monthly_avg_rate
    FROM historical_electricity_rates her
    WHERE her.effective_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 years'
    GROUP BY her.utility_id, her.rate_code_id, her.state_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', her.effective_date)
),
trend_calculation AS (
    SELECT
        hrt.*,
        LAG(hrt.monthly_avg_rate, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY hrt.utility_id, hrt.rate_code_id ORDER BY hrt.rate_month) AS prev_rate,
        LEAD(hrt.monthly_avg_rate, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY hrt.utility_id, hrt.rate_code_id ORDER BY hrt.rate_month) AS next_rate,
        AVG(hrt.monthly_avg_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY hrt.utility_id, hrt.rate_code_id ORDER BY hrt.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_12mo
    FROM historical_rate_trends hrt
),
forecast_models AS (
    SELECT
        tc.*,
        tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate AS monthly_change,
        AVG(tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY tc.utility_id, tc.rate_code_id ORDER BY tc.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_monthly_change,
        tc.monthly_avg_rate + (AVG(tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY tc.utility_id, tc.rate_code_id ORDER BY tc.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) * 6) AS forecast_6mo,
        tc.monthly_avg_rate + (AVG(tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY tc.utility_id, tc.rate_code_id ORDER BY tc.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) * 12) AS forecast_12mo
    FROM trend_calculation tc
    WHERE tc.prev_rate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    utility_id, rate_code_id, state_id, rate_month,
    ROUND(CAST(monthly_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS monthly_avg_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(prev_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS prev_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(monthly_change AS NUMERIC), 6) AS monthly_change,
    ROUND(CAST(avg_monthly_change AS NUMERIC), 6) AS avg_monthly_change,
    ROUND(CAST(forecast_6mo AS NUMERIC), 6) AS forecast_6mo,
    ROUND(CAST(forecast_12mo AS NUMERIC), 6) AS forecast_12mo
FROM forecast_models
WHERE rate_month >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months'
ORDER BY utility_id, rate_code_id, rate_month DESC;

db-15.title: Utility Rate Strategy Analysis with Rate Code Portfolio Optimization

db-15.sql:
WITH utility_portfolio_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        uc.utility_id,
        uc.utility_name,
        uc.state_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_code_id) AS rate_codes_offered,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_id) AS total_rates,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS portfolio_avg_rate,
        STDDEV(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS portfolio_rate_stddev
    FROM utility_companies uc
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er ON uc.utility_id = er.utility_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY uc.utility_id, uc.utility_name, uc.state_id
),
portfolio_optimization AS (
    SELECT
        upa.*,
        CASE
            WHEN upa.rate_codes_offered >= 5 AND upa.portfolio_rate_stddev > upa.portfolio_avg_rate * 0.1 THEN 'Well Diversified'
            WHEN upa.rate_codes_offered >= 3 THEN 'Moderately Diversified'
            ELSE 'Limited Diversification'
        END AS diversification_status,
        CASE
            WHEN upa.rate_codes_offered < 3 THEN 'Consider Adding Rate Codes'
            WHEN upa.portfolio_rate_stddev < upa.portfolio_avg_rate * 0.05 THEN 'Consider Rate Differentiation'
            ELSE 'Portfolio Optimized'
        END AS optimization_recommendation
    FROM utility_portfolio_analysis upa
)
SELECT
    utility_id, utility_name, state_id,
    rate_codes_offered, total_rates,
    ROUND(CAST(portfolio_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS portfolio_avg_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(portfolio_rate_stddev AS NUMERIC), 6) AS portfolio_rate_stddev,

FROM portfolio_optimization
ORDER BY state_id, utility_name;

WITH incentive_availability AS (

    LEFT JOIN utility_incentives ui ON s.state_id = ui.state_id AND ui.is_active = TRUE AND (ui.expiration_date IS NULL OR ui.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE)
    GROUP BY s.state_id, s.state_name, s.region
),
market_coverage_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        ia.*,
        (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT utility_id) FROM utility_companies WHERE state_id = ia.state_id AND is_active = TRUE) AS total_utilities_in_state,
        CASE
            WHEN (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT utility_id) FROM utility_companies WHERE state_id = ia.state_id AND is_active = TRUE) > 0 THEN
                (ia.utilities_with_incentives::NUMERIC / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT utility_id) FROM utility_companies WHERE state_id = ia.state_id AND is_active = TRUE)) * 100
            ELSE 0
        END AS utility_coverage_percentage
    FROM incentive_availability ia
)
SELECT
    state_id, state_name, region,
    federal_incentives_available, state_incentives_available, utility_incentives_available,
    utilities_with_incentives, total_utilities_in_state,
    ROUND(CAST(utility_coverage_percentage AS NUMERIC), 2) AS utility_coverage_percentage
FROM market_coverage_analysis
ORDER BY utility_coverage_percentage DESC, state_name;

)

db-15.complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), performance analysis, efficiency metrics, performance evaluation, aggregations

db-15.sql:
WITH rate_structure_performance AS (
    SELECT
        rs.rate_structure_id,
        rs.utility_id,
        rs.rate_code_id,
        er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh,
        er.fixed_charge_usd,
        er.demand_charge_usd_per_kw,
        COUNT(DISTINCT trt.tier_id) AS tier_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT tou.tou_period_id) AS tou_period_count
    FROM rate_structures rs
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er ON rs.rate_structure_id = er.rate_structure_id
    LEFT JOIN tiered_rate_tiers trt ON rs.rate_structure_id = trt.rate_structure_id
    LEFT JOIN time_of_use_periods tou ON rs.rate_structure_id = tou.rate_structure_id
    WHERE rs.is_current = TRUE AND er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY rs.rate_structure_id, rs.utility_id, rs.rate_code_id, er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh, er.fixed_charge_usd, er.demand_charge_usd_per_kw
),
efficiency_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        rsp.*,
        (rsp.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh * 1000) + COALESCE(rsp.fixed_charge_usd, 0) + COALESCE(rsp.demand_charge_usd_per_kw, 0) AS total_cost_per_1000kwh,
        CASE
            WHEN rsp.tier_count > 0 OR rsp.tou_period_count > 0 THEN 'Complex Structure'
            ELSE 'Simple Structure'
        END AS structure_complexity
    FROM rate_structure_performance rsp
)
SELECT
    rate_structure_id, utility_id, rate_code_id,
    ROUND(CAST(energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS NUMERIC), 6) AS energy_charge_usd_per_kwh,
    ROUND(CAST(fixed_charge_usd AS NUMERIC), 2) AS fixed_charge_usd,
    ROUND(CAST(demand_charge_usd_per_kw AS NUMERIC), 4) AS demand_charge_usd_per_kw,
    tier_count, tou_period_count,

    structure_complexity
FROM efficiency_metrics
ORDER BY total_cost_per_1000kwh;

db-15.title: Recursive Rate Code Hierarchy Analysis with Multi-Level Rate Structure Traversal
db-15.description: Description: Enterprise-level recursive rate code hierarchy analysis using recursive CTE for multi-level rate structure traversal, hierarchy relationships, and comprehensive hierarchy analysis. Demonstrates production patterns used by hierarchy analysis platforms and recursive traversal systems. Use Case: Hierarchy Analysis Platform - Multi-Level Rate Structure Traversal for Rate Design Engineers Business Value: Comprehensive recursive rate code hierarchy analysis showing multi-level structures,
db-15.complexity: Advanced recursive CTE (6+ levels), hierarchy traversal, multi-level analysis, recursive relationships, cycle detection
db-15.expected_output: Recursive rate code hierarchy analysis with multi-level traversal.
db-15.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE rate_code_hierarchy AS (
    SELECT
        rc.rate_code_id AS parent_code_id,
        rc.rate_code AS parent_code,
        rc.rate_code_category,
        rc2.rate_code_id AS child_code_id,
        rc2.rate_code AS child_code,
        1 AS hierarchy_level,
        ARRAY[rc.rate_code_id] AS code_path
    FROM rate_codes rc
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc2 ON rc.rate_code_category = rc2.rate_code_category AND rc.rate_code_id != rc2.rate_code_id
    WHERE rc.is_active = TRUE AND rc2.is_active = TRUE
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT
        rch.parent_code_id,
        rch.parent_code,
        rch.rate_code_category,
        rc3.rate_code_id,
        rc3.rate_code,
        rch.hierarchy_level + 1,
        rch.code_path || ARRAY[rc3.rate_code_id]
    FROM rate_code_hierarchy rch
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc3 ON rch.rate_code_category = rc3.rate_code_category
    WHERE rch.hierarchy_level < 5
        AND NOT rc3.rate_code_id = ANY(rch.code_path)
),
hierarchy_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        rch.*,
        array_length(rch.code_path, 1) AS path_length,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY rch.parent_code_id) AS total_children
    FROM rate_code_hierarchy rch
)
SELECT
    parent_code_id, parent_code, child_code_id, child_code,
    rate_code_category, hierarchy_level, path_length, total_children
FROM hierarchy_analysis
ORDER BY parent_code, hierarchy_level;
